A01: Taking all things together, how would you say things are these days--would you say you're very happy, pretty happy, or not too happy these days?
A02: Looking ahead to the next five years, do you think that things in this country will get better or worse?
A03: Looking ahead to the next five years, do you think that things in the rest of the world will get better or worse?
A04: How do you think your own life will go in the next five years--do you think it will get better or worse?

A05: Some people think a lot about the social problems of the nation and the world, and about how they might be solved. Others spend little time thinking about these issues. How much do you think about such things?

A06: These questions are about pollution and the environment. Please mark the circle that shows how much you agree or disagree with each statement below. A06a: In general, pollution has increased in the U.S. in the last ten years
A06b: The dangers of pollution are not really as great as government, the media, and environmental groups would like us to believe
A06c: America needs growth to survive, and that is going to require some increase in pollution
A06d: People will have to change their buying habits and way of life to correct our environmental problems
A06e: Government should take action to solve our environmental problems even if it means that some of the products we now use would have to be changed or banned
A06f: Government should place higher taxes on products which cause pollution in their manufacture or disposal, so that companies will be encouraged to find better ways to produce them
A06g: I wish that government would ban throwaway bottles and beverage cans
A06h: T.V. commercials stimulate people to buy a lot of things they don't really need
A06i: T.V. commercials do a lot of good by showing new products that we might not know about otherwise
A06j: My family and I often buy things we don't really need; we could get along with much less
A06k: By the year 2000, engineers and scientists will probably have invented devices that will solve our pollution problems
A07: In your own actions--the things you buy and the things you do--how much of an effort do you make to conserve energy and protect the environment?

A08: Different people may look for different things in their work. Below is a list of some of these things. Please read each one, then indicate how important this thing is for you. A08a: A job where you can see the results of what you do
A08b: A job that has high status and prestige
A08c: A job which is interesting to do
A08d: A job where the chances for advancement and promotion are good
A08e: A job that gives you an opportunity to be directly helpful to others
A08f: A job which provides you with a chance to earn a good deal of money
A08g: A job where you have the chance to be creative
A08h: A job where the skills you learn will not go out of date
A08i: A job that gives you a chance to make friends
A08j: A job which uses your skills and abilities--lets you do the things you can do best
A08k: A job that is worthwhile to society
A08l: A job where you have more than two weeks vacation
A08m: A job where you get a chance to participate in decision making
A08n: A job which leaves a lot of time for other things in your life
A08o: A job which allows you to establish roots in a community and not have to move from place to place
A08p: A job which leaves you mostly free of supervision by others
A08q: A job that offers a reasonably predictable, secure future
A08r: A job where you can learn new things, learn new skills
A08s: A job where you do not have to pretend to be a type of person that you are not
A08t: A job that most people look up to and respect
A08u: A job that permits contact with a lot of people
A08v: A job with an easy pace that lets you work slowly
A08w: A job where most problems are quite difficult and challenging

B10: Amphetamines have been prescribed by doctors to help people lose weight or to give people more energy. They are Sometimes called uppers, ups, speed, bennies, dexies, pep pills, and diet pills. Amphetamines do NOT include any non-prescription drugs, such as over-the-counter diet pills (like Dexatrim (R)) or stay-awake pills (like No-Doz (R)), or any mail-order drugs. On how many occasions (if any) have you taken amphetamines on your own--that is, without a doctor telling you to take them... B10a: [Amphetamines]...in your lifetime [not under doctor's orders]?
